children.title: 01_company_overview.docx
children.summary: This document provides an overview of Meridian Dynamics Corp (MDC), an industrial technology company founded in 2009 that designs, manufactures, and services precision automation equipment for the aerospace, automotive, and renewable-energy sectors. Headquartered in Austin, Texas, with regional offices in Chicago, Illinois, and Krakow, Poland, MDC employs approximately 2,400 people and generated $412 million in revenue in its most recent fiscal year across its four business units: Industrial Automation, Renewable Systems, Aftermarket Services, and Digital Solutions. Led by CEO Tom Reyes—who holds capital expenditure sign-off authority above $250,000—and an executive team including CFO Sarah Chen, VP of Engineering Marcus Webb, and General Counsel Elena Petrova, MDC maintains a documentation-heavy culture, which motivated the Digital Solutions unit to invest in retrieval-augmented knowledge systems. Additionally, the document outlines key strategic initiatives, including Marcus Webb's cloud infrastructure migration (Project Helios) aiming to reduce data-center operating costs by 30% and Linda Fischer's ERP system rollout (Project Atlas), while detailing the company's escalation protocols and geographic distribution across its Austin (~1,050 employees), Chicago (~900 employees), and Krakow (~450 employees) facilities.

children.title: About Us
children.summary: Meridian Dynamics Corp (MDC), founded in 2009 and headquartered in Austin, Texas, with regional offices in Chicago, Illinois, and Krakow, Poland, is an industrial technology company that designs, manufactures, and services precision automation equipment for the aerospace, automotive, and renewable-energy sectors. Employing approximately 2,400 people worldwide with a reported revenue of $412 million in its most recently completed fiscal year, MDC is structured into four business units: Industrial Automation, Renewable Systems, Aftermarket Services, and Digital Solutions. The Digital Solutions unit is the newest business unit and houses the company's internal software and data initiatives, including the enterprise knowledge platform supported by this document set.
children.full_text:
Meridian Dynamics Corp (MDC) is a mid-sized industrial technology company headquartered in Austin, Texas, with regional offices in Chicago, Illinois and Krakow, Poland. Founded in 2009, the company designs, manufactures, and services precision automation equipment for the aerospace, automotive, and renewable-energy sectors. MDC employs approximately 2,400 people worldwide and reported revenue of $412 million in the most recently completed fiscal year.
The company is organized into four primary business units: Industrial Automation, Renewable Systems, Aftermarket Services, and Digital Solutions. Digital Solutions, the newest business unit, was formed to house the company's internal software and data initiatives, including the enterprise knowledge platform this document set supports.

children.title: Leadership
children.summary: Meridian Dynamics is led by Chief Executive Officer Tom Reyes, who joined the company in 2018, reports to the Board of Directors, and holds sign-off authority on capital expenditures above $250,000. Six executives report directly to Reyes: Chief Financial Officer Sarah Chen (overseeing Finance, Procurement, and Financial Planning & Analysis), Vice President of Engineering Marcus Webb (overseeing product engineering, IT infrastructure, and IT Security), General Counsel Elena Petrova (overseeing Legal, Contracts, and Compliance), and the heads of the four business units. The complete executive reporting structure is detailed in the organizational chart referenced as 09_org_chart_and_roles.
children.full_text:
Meridian Dynamics is led by Chief Executive Officer Tom Reyes, who joined the company in 2018 after previously serving as COO of a competing firm. Reyes reports to the Board of Directors and holds ultimate sign-off authority on all capital expenditures above $250,000.

Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer, overseeing Finance, Procurement, and Financial Planning & Analysis.

children.title: Culture and Ways of Working
children.summary: At Meridian Dynamics, daily knowledge-sharing challenges and search inefficiencies, such as engineers looking through shared drives, old emails, and outdated wikis, motivated the Digital Solutions unit to invest in retrieval-augmented knowledge systems. The company maintains a culture heavily focused on written documentation, where employees must consult specific written policies for recurring decisions—including hiring, procurement, security exceptions, and vendor onboarding—prior to escalating questions to managers or subject-matter experts.
children.full_text:
Employees at Meridian Dynamics frequently describe the company's internal knowledge-sharing challenges as a major source of daily friction. Engineers report spending significant portions of their week searching through shared drives, old email threads, and outdated wikis to find information that technically already exists somewhere in the organization. This inefficiency was a primary motivator behind the Digital Solutions unit's investment in retrieval-augmented knowledge systems.
The company values written documentation. Nearly every recurring decision — hiring, procurement, security exceptions, vendor onboarding — is governed by a written policy. Employees are expected to consult the relevant policy before escalating a question to a manager or subject-matter expert.

children.title: Strategic Initiatives
children.summary: The Strategic Initiatives document details two major internal projects: Project Helios, a multi-year cloud infrastructure migration led by Marcus Webb of the Engineering organization aiming to transition on-premises compute workloads to the cloud and reduce data-center operating costs by an estimated 30%, and Project Atlas, an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system rollout led by Linda Fischer (VP of Finance Operations) to replace decade-old financial and inventory systems. Both initiatives depend on external vendors for hardware, software licensing, and logistics support, and both are subject to the company's standard procurement approval workflow referenced in 05_project_approval_workflow.
children.full_text:
Two major internal initiatives are currently underway:
Project Helios — a multi-year cloud infrastructure migration led by the Engineering organization under Marcus Webb, intended to move the majority of on-premises compute workloads to cloud infrastructure and reduce data-center operating costs by an estimated 30%.
Project Atlas — an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system rollout led by the Finance organization under Linda Fischer, VP of Finance Operations, intended to replace the company's decade-old financial and inventory systems.
Both initiatives rely on external vendors for hardware, software licensing, and logistics support, and both are subject to the company's standard procurement approval workflow (see 05_project_approval_workflow).

children.title: 02_hr_policy_manual.docx
children.summary: The Meridian Dynamics HR Policy Manual establishes the company's official guidelines governing employment basics, leave, benefits, conduct, performance, and separation. Under Section 1, employees are classified as Full-Time (working 35+ hours per week), Part-Time, or Temporary/Contract, with new full-time hires undergoing a 90-day probationary period and select departments (Engineering, Digital Solutions, and Finance) qualifying for a hybrid remote schedule. Section 2 details the leave policy, covering tenure-based PTO accruals (15 to 25 days annually with a 10-day carryover limit, except in select Polish jurisdictions), 10 annual sick days, gender-neutral parental leave (16 weeks for primary caregivers, 6 weeks for secondary caregivers), and bereavement leave. Section 3 outlines employee benefits, including company-subsidized health insurance, a dollar-for-dollar 401(k) or pension match up to 4% of base salary, and a $1,500 annual professional development budget. The Section 4 Code of Conduct mandates conflict-of-interest disclosures to Compliance Officer Aisha Malik, legal clearance from Elena Petrova's team for disclosing confidential info, and reporting harassment to HR (James Okoro), Aisha Malik, or an ethics hotline. Finally, the manual details bi-annual performance reviews in June and December—which can lead to a 60-day Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) for underperforming employees—and separation procedures, requiring 2 to 4 weeks' notice for voluntary resignations and ensuring final paychecks are delivered by the next standard pay cycle.

children.title: 1. Employment Basics
children.summary: Under Section 1, Employment Basics, Meridian Dynamics classifies employees as Full-Time (35+ hours/week, which determines Section 3 benefits eligibility), Part-Time (fewer than 35 hours/week), or Temporary/Contract. New full-time employees undergo a 90-calendar-day probationary period from their start date, during which either the employee or Meridian Dynamics can terminate employment with 5 business days' notice instead of the standard Section 6.2 notice. Standard work hours are 9:00 AM to 5:30 PM local time, Monday through Friday. Employees in Engineering, Digital Solutions, and Finance are eligible for a hybrid schedule of up to 3 remote days per week subject to manager approval, while Aftermarket Services and Manufacturing roles are generally ineligible for remote work due to on-site equipment requirements.
children.full_text:
1.1 Employment Classification
Employees are classified as Full-Time (35+ hours/week), Part-Time (fewer than 35 hours/week), or Temporary/Contract. Classification determines eligibility for benefits described in Section 3.
1.2 Probationary Period
All new full-time employees serve a 90-calendar-day probationary period beginning on their start date. During this period, either the employee or Meridian Dynamics may terminate employment with 5 business days' notice, rather than the standard notice period described in Section 6.2.
1.3 Work Hours and Remote Work
Standard work hours are 9:00 AM to 5:30 PM local time, Monday through Friday. Employees in Engineering, Digital Solutions, and Finance are eligible for a hybrid schedule of up to 3 remote days per week, subject to manager approval. Aftermarket Services and Manufacturing roles are generally not eligible for remote work due to on-site equipment requirements.

children.title: 2. Leave Policy
children.summary: This section details the Meridian Dynamics Leave Policy, covering Paid Time Off (PTO), sick leave, parental leave, and bereavement leave. Full-time employees accrue PTO monthly based on tenure, receiving 15 days per year for Years 0–2, 20 days for Years 3–5, and 25 days for Years 6+, with a maximum carryover of 10 unused days into the next calendar year unless prohibited by local law (e.g., select jurisdictions in Poland). Additionally, employees receive 10 non-carryover paid sick days per calendar year. The policy provides gender-neutral paid parental leave for births, adoptions, or foster placements to be taken within 12 months of the event, offering 16 weeks for primary caregivers and 6 weeks for secondary caregivers. Lastly, paid bereavement leave is granted at 5 days for immediate family members and 2 days for extended family.
children.full_text:
2.1 Paid Time Off (PTO)
Full-time employees accrue PTO at the following rates based on tenure:
Years 0–2: 15 days per year
Years 3–5: 20 days per year
Years 6+: 25 days per year
PTO accrues monthly and may be carried over up to a maximum of 10 unused days into the following calendar year. Unused PTO beyond this cap is forfeited, except where prohibited by local law (e.g., certain jurisdictions in Poland).
2.2 Sick Leave
Employees receive 10 paid sick days per calendar year, separate from PTO. Sick leave does not carry over year to year.
2.3 Parental Leave
Meridian Dynamics provides 16 weeks of paid parental leave for the primary caregiver and 6 weeks for the secondary caregiver, regardless of gender, for births, adoptions, or foster placements. Parental leave must be taken within 12 months of the qualifying event.
2.4 Bereavement Leave
Employees are entitled to 5 paid days of bereavement leave for the death of an immediate family member, and 2 paid days for extended family.

children.title: 3. Benefits
children.summary: Under Section 3 (Benefits), Meridian Dynamics provides full-time employees with company-subsidized health insurance starting the first day of the month following their start date, covering 80% of employee-only premiums and 60% of dependent premiums. For retirement savings, the company matches employee 401(k) or local-equivalent pension contributions dollar-for-dollar up to 4% of base salary, which vests immediately. Additionally, employees receive an annual professional development budget of $1,500 USD (or local currency equivalent) for manager-approved courses, certifications, or conferences.

children.title: 4. Code of Conduct
children.summary: This section of the Meridian Dynamics Code of Conduct outlines policies regarding conflicts of interest, confidentiality, and anti-harassment. Section 4.1 requires employees to disclose any financial or personal relationships with current or prospective vendors, suppliers (including those referenced in the Supply Chain Network document), or customers to their manager and Compliance Officer Aisha Malik before engaging in business dealings. Section 4.2 enforces confidentiality obligations for company financial data, unreleased product designs, and vendor contract terms, requiring written approval from Legal (Elena Petrova's organization) prior to any external disclosure. Section 4.3 establishes a zero-tolerance policy for harassment or discrimination, directing reports to HR (James Okoro), Compliance (Aisha Malik), or the anonymous ethics hotline.
children.full_text:
4.1 Conflicts of Interest
Employees must disclose any financial or personal relationship with a current or prospective vendor, supplier, or customer to their manager and to the Compliance Officer (Aisha Malik) before engaging in any business dealings with that party. This includes relationships with vendors such as those described in the Supply Chain Network document.
4.2 Confidentiality
All employees are bound by the confidentiality terms in their employment agreement. Company financial data, unreleased product designs, and vendor contract terms are considered confidential and may not be disclosed outside the company without written approval from Legal (Elena Petrova's organization).
4.3 Anti-Harassment
Meridian Dynamics maintains a zero-tolerance policy for harassment or discrimination of any kind. Reports may be made to HR (James Okoro), Compliance (Aisha Malik), or through the anonymous ethics hotline.

Employees who receive a "Needs Improvement" rating are placed on a 60-day Performance Improvement Plan (PIP), which is jointly designed by their direct manager and an HR Business Partner (Section 5.2).

children.title: 6. Separation from Employment
children.summary: This section details the procedures and requirements for separation from employment. For voluntary resignations (Section 6.1), employees must provide a minimum of 2 weeks' written notice, which increases to 4 weeks for those at the Director level or above. Involuntary termination (Section 6.2) outside of the probationary period (defined in Section 1.2) requires documented performance or conduct issues, an HR review, and sign-off from the department head. Finally, Section 6.3 outlines that final paychecks, including any accrued and unused PTO, must be issued no later than the next standard pay cycle following the separation date, or sooner if mandated by local law.

6.3 Final Pay and Benefits

children.title: 03_it_security_policy.docx
children.summary: This IT Security Policy establishes the rules for the acceptable use, protection, and management of Meridian Dynamics Corp's information systems, specifically focusing on Project Helios and Project Atlas. The policy applies to all employees, contractors, and vendors—including cloud infrastructure provider Acme Cloud Solutions and physical component supplier Bright Steel Supply—and mandates strict account management, including 14-character minimum password requirements, regular password rotation, mandatory multi-factor authentication (MFA) for remote or administrative access, and the revocation of terminated employee access within 4 business hours. Third-party vendors are categorized into three risk tiers, requiring Tier 1 high-risk vendors (such as Acme Cloud Solutions) to undergo annual SOC 2 Type II audit reviews and obtain annual re-approval from David Osei (IT Security) and Aisha Malik (Compliance). Data is classified into four levels with strict encryption and authorization requirements, including specific Project Helios guidelines that mandate environment segregation, AES-256 and TLS 1.2 or higher encryption, and monthly cloud spend and access reviews by IT Security and Priya Raman (Procurement). Finally, security incidents must be reported within 1 hour, with critical incidents escalated to CEO Tom Reyes and General Counsel Elena Petrova within 4 hours, and any exceptions to these policies require written risk acceptance signed by the requesting department head and David Osei, with a copy sent to Aisha Malik.

It applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party vendors with access to company systems, including vendors such as Acme Cloud Solutions.

children.title: 2. Account and Access Management
children.summary: This section details the company's account and access management policies. Section 2.1 establishes password requirements of at least 14 characters, complexity (one uppercase, lowercase, number, and symbol), and a 10-password history limit. Section 2.2 mandates password rotation every 180 days for standard users and every 90 days for privileged/administrative accounts, including Acme Cloud Solutions cloud administrator accounts. Under Section 2.3, Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is mandatory for remote access, administrative accounts, and systems classified as "Confidential" or "Restricted" under Section 4.2. Section 2.4 requires department managers to review team access rights every 6 months and mandates the revocation of terminated employee access within 4 business hours of HR system registration.
children.full_text:
2.1 Password Requirements
All company accounts must use passwords meeting the following criteria:
Minimum 14 characters
At least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one number, and one symbol
Must not reuse any of the previous 10 passwords
2.2 Password Rotation
Passwords for standard user accounts must be rotated every 180 days. Passwords for privileged/administrative accounts, including cloud administrator accounts used to manage Acme Cloud Solutions infrastructure, must be rotated every 90 days.
2.3 Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
MFA is mandatory for all remote access, all administrative accounts, and all access to systems classified as "Confidential" or "Restricted" under Section 4.2.
2.4 Access Review
Department managers must review and certify their team's system access rights every 6 months. Access for terminated employees must be revoked within 4 business hours of the separation being recorded in the HR system.

children.title: 3. Vendor and Third-Party Access
children.summary: Under the vendor and third-party access policy, vendors are classified into three risk tiers based on data sensitivity: Tier 1 (High Risk) for vendors accessing Confidential or Restricted data (such as cloud infrastructure provider Acme Cloud Solutions); Tier 2 (Medium Risk) for vendors with access to Internal-only data; and Tier 3 (Low Risk) for those with no system access (such as physical component supplier Bright Steel Supply). Tier 1 vendors must meet strict compliance obligations, including undergoing an annual SOC 2 Type II audit review, signing a Data Processing Agreement, and obtaining annual re-approval from IT Security (David Osei) and Compliance (Aisha Malik). Acme Cloud Solutions was last re-approved under these requirements as documented in the vendor contract reference 04_vendor_contract_acme.
children.full_text:
3.1 Vendor Risk Tiers
Vendors are classified into three risk tiers based on the sensitivity of data they can access:
Tier 1 (High Risk): Vendors with access to Confidential or Restricted data (e.g., cloud infrastructure providers such as Acme Cloud Solutions).
Tier 2 (Medium Risk): Vendors with access to Internal-only data.
Tier 3 (Low Risk): Vendors with no system access (e.g., hardware suppliers such as Bright Steel Supply who ship physical components without network access).
3.2 Tier 1 Vendor Requirements
Tier 1 vendors must undergo an annual SOC 2 Type II audit review, sign a Data Processing Agreement, and be re-approved by both IT Security (David Osei) and Compliance (Aisha Malik) annually. Acme Cloud Solutions was last re-approved under this process as documented in the vendor contract (see 04_vendor_contract_acme).

children.title: 4. Data Classification
children.summary: At Meridian Dynamics, data is classified into four levels with specific handling requirements: Public data has no distribution restrictions, while Internal data requires manager approval for external sharing. Confidential data—encompassing financial reports, vendor contracts, and employee records—demands encryption at rest and in transit, with access limited to named individuals or roles. Restricted data—which includes trade secrets, unreleased product designs, and security incident details—requires multi-factor authentication (MFA), encryption, and explicit access-list approval from the Director of IT Security.
children.full_text:
4.1 Classification Levels
Data at Meridian Dynamics is classified into four levels: Public, Internal, Confidential, and Restricted.
4.2 Handling Requirements by Level
Public: No restrictions on distribution.
Internal: May be shared within the company but not externally without manager approval.
Confidential: Includes financial reports, vendor contracts, and employee records. Requires encryption at rest and in transit, and access is limited to named individuals or roles.
Restricted: Includes trade secrets, unreleased product designs, and security incident details. Requires MFA, encryption, and explicit access-list approval from the Director of IT Security.

children.title: 5. Incident Response
children.summary: Under the "5. Incident Response" policy, suspected security incidents must be reported to the IT Security team or David Osei's team within 1 hour of discovery through the internal incident portal. Incidents are classified as Low, Medium, High, or Critical based on data sensitivity and impact, with Critical incidents requiring notification to CEO Tom Reyes and General Counsel Elena Petrova within 4 hours. Additionally, all High and Critical incidents require a formal post-incident review within 10 business days, coordinated jointly by the IT Security and Compliance teams.

5.2 Severity Classification
Incidents are classified as Low, Medium, High, or Critical based on data sensitivity and scope of impact. Critical incidents require notification to the CEO (Tom Reyes) and General Counsel (Elena Petrova) within 4 hours.
5.3 Post-Incident Review
All High and Critical incidents require a formal post-incident review within 10 business days, coordinated jointly by IT Security and Compliance.

children.title: 6. Cloud Infrastructure Security (Project Helios Specific)
children.summary: This section details the cloud infrastructure security requirements specific to Project Helios hosted with Acme Cloud Solutions. It mandates strict environment segregation among development, staging, and production, with production access restricted to a named list approved by David Osei. All data must be encrypted utilizing AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.2 or higher in transit, and cloud spend and access logs must undergo monthly reviews by IT Security and Procurement (Priya Raman) to identify anomalous usage or unauthorized provisioning.
children.full_text:
6.1 Environment Segregation
Project Helios cloud environments hosted with Acme Cloud Solutions must maintain strict segregation between development, staging, and production environments, with production access limited to a named list approved by David Osei.
6.2 Encryption Standards
All data stored in Acme Cloud Solutions environments must be encrypted using AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.2 or higher in transit.
6.3 Cost and Access Monitoring
Cloud spend and access logs for Project Helios infrastructure are reviewed monthly by IT Security in coordination with Procurement (Priya Raman) to detect anomalous usage or unauthorized provisioning.

children.title: Article 1 — Scope of Services
children.full_text:
Acme Cloud Solutions shall provide cloud compute, storage, and managed database services in support of
Meridian Dynamics Corp's Project Helios cloud migration initiative, as further detailed in Exhibit A
(Statement of Work).

children.title: Article 2 — Fees and Payment
children.full_text:
2.1 Total contract value is estimated at $3,200,000 over the initial 3-year term, based on projected usage
tiers.
2.2 Invoices are issued monthly in arrears and payable net-30.
2.3 Any single change order or usage commitment exceeding $50,000 requires written approval per
Meridian Dynamics Corp's internal Purchase Approval Workflow (see 05_project_approval_workflow) prior
to execution.

children.title: Article 3 — Service Level Agreement (SLA)
children.full_text:
3.1 Acme Cloud Solutions guarantees 99.95% monthly uptime for production workloads.
3.2 Service credits of 5% of monthly fees are issued for each 0.1% shortfall below the guaranteed uptime,
up to a maximum of 50% of monthly fees in any billing period.
3.3 Planned maintenance windows require 7 days' advance notice.

children.title: Article 4 — Security and Compliance
children.full_text:
4.1 Acme Cloud Solutions is classified as a Tier 1 (High Risk) vendor under Meridian Dynamics Corp's IT
Security Policy (SEC-POL-004), Section 3.1.
4.2 Vendor shall undergo an annual SOC 2 Type II audit and provide the audit report to Meridian Dynamics
Corp's IT Security team (David Osei) within 30 days of completion.
4.3 Vendor shall maintain encryption standards consistent with Section 6.2 of Meridian Dynamics Corp's IT
Security Policy (AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit).
4.4 This agreement was most recently re-approved on the annual review cycle by David Osei (IT Security)
and Aisha Malik (Compliance) as of the current fiscal year's Q1 vendor review.

children.title: Article 5 — Data Processing
children.full_text:
5.1 A separate Data Processing Agreement (DPA), attached as Exhibit B, governs the handling of any
personal data processed through Acme Cloud Solutions infrastructure.
5.2 Data residency for European operations (supporting the Krakow office) is limited to EU-based data
centers.

children.title: Article 6 — Termination
children.full_text:
6.1 Either party may terminate for material breach with 30 days' written notice and opportunity to cure.
6.2 Meridian Dynamics Corp may terminate for convenience with 90 days' written notice, subject to
early-termination fees described in Exhibit C.

children.title: Article 7 — Renewal and Amendment History
children.full_text:
7.1 This contract's most recent amendment (Amendment No. 2) was executed to expand storage capacity in
support of Project Helios's Phase 2 rollout, increasing the annual committed spend by $410,000.
7.2 Amendment No. 2 was approved through the standard approval chain: Priya Raman (Procurement) ->
Sarah Chen (CFO) -> Tom Reyes (CEO), consistent with the $50,000 threshold rule in Article 2.3.

children.title: 1. Purpose
children.full_text: This document defines the approval chain required for purchase commitments, vendor contracts, and project budget allocations at Meridian Dynamics Corp. It applies to all business units, including Project Helios (Engineering) and Project Atlas (Finance).

children.title: 3. Standard Approval Chain (the "$50k Rule")
children.full_text:
Any single purchase order, contract, or change order valued at $50,000 or more must be routed through the following sequence before execution:
Priya Raman, Head of Procurement — validates vendor selection, pricing, and Tier classification (per IT Security Policy Section 3.1 if the vendor has system access).
Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer — validates budget availability and financial terms.
Tom Reyes, Chief Executive Officer — final sign-off authority.
This chain applies regardless of business unit, and was used for both the original Acme Cloud Solutions master agreement and its subsequent Amendment No. 2 (see 04_vendor_contract_acme, Article 7).

children.title: 4. Special Cases
children.full_text:
4.1 IT Security-Relevant Purchases
Any purchase involving a vendor that will receive system access (Tier 1 or Tier 2 under the IT Security Policy) requires an additional sign-off from David Osei, Director of IT Security, inserted between steps 1 and 2 of the Standard Approval Chain in Section 3.
4.2 Legal Review Requirement
Any new vendor contract (not a renewal or amendment of an existing contract) requires review by Elena Petrova, General Counsel, prior to Priya Raman's step in the Standard Approval Chain.
4.3 Capital Expenditure Above $250,000
Per company policy, capital expenditures above $250,000 require Tom Reyes's sign-off as CEO regardless of business unit, consistent with his authority described in the Company Overview document.

children.title: 1. Overview
children.full_text:
The HX-7200 Precision Actuator Controller is a rack-mounted control unit used to drive high-precision servo
actuators in automated manufacturing lines. This manual covers installation, configuration, and
troubleshooting for firmware versions 3.0 through 3.2.

children.title: 2. Installation
children.full_text:
2.1 Mounting Requirements
The HX-7200 must be mounted in a standard 19-inch rack enclosure with a minimum of 2U clearance above
and below the unit for airflow. Operating temperature range is 0°C to 45°C; ambient temperature above
45°C will trigger the thermal-protection shutdown described in Section 5.3.
2.2 Power Requirements
The unit requires a 24V DC input, rated at a maximum draw of 6.5A under full load. Use only the
MDC-approved PSU-2400 power supply; use of third-party supplies voids the warranty described in Section
8.
2.3 Network Configuration
The HX-7200 supports both EtherCAT and Modbus TCP for host communication. Default IP configuration is
DHCP; static IP assignment is configured via the front-panel keypad under Menu -> Network -> Static IP.

children.title: 3. Configuration
children.full_text:
3.1 Axis Calibration
Each of the controller's up to 4 axes must be calibrated individually using the auto-tune procedure: Menu ->
Axis Config -> Auto-Tune. Auto-tune should be repeated any time the connected actuator or load mass
changes by more than 15%.
3.2 Safety Limits
Soft limits (software-enforced travel limits) must be configured for every axis before enabling motion. Hard
limits (physical limit switches) are mandatory and cannot be disabled through software, per the safety
requirements in Section 6.
3.3 PID Tuning Parameters
Default PID values (P=1.2, I=0.05, D=0.01) are suitable for most standard loads. For high-inertia loads,
increase the D term incrementally in steps of 0.01 while monitoring for oscillation.

children.title: 4. Diagnostic Codes
children.full_text:
Code
Meaning
Recommended Action
E-101
Overtemperature shutdown
Verify rack airflow; check ambient temp against Section 2.1
E-204
Encoder signal loss
Check encoder cabling; verify connector seating
E-317
Overcurrent on axis N
Reduce load or verify mechanical binding
E-450
Network communication timeout
Verify EtherCAT/Modbus cabling and host configuration
E-512
Calibration data corrupted
Re-run auto-tune per Section 3.1

children.title: 5. Maintenance
children.full_text:
5.1 Firmware Updates
Firmware updates are applied via USB using the MDC Configuration Utility. Always back up axis calibration
data before updating firmware, as updates from version 2.x to 3.x require recalibration.
5.2 Preventive Maintenance Schedule
Inspect connector seating and rack airflow every 6 months. Replace the internal cooling fan every 3 years or
upon detection of fan-speed warnings in the diagnostic log.
5.3 Thermal Protection
If internal temperature exceeds 70°C, the unit automatically disables motor output and displays error code
E-101 until the unit cools below 60°C.

children.title: 6. Safety Requirements
children.full_text:
Hard limit switches must be installed and wired to the dedicated safety input terminals (SI1–SI4) on every
axis. The HX-7200 is rated to Category 3 (per applicable machine safety standards) only when hard limits
are correctly wired; without them, the unit must be treated as Category B (no independent safety rating).

children.title: 7. Ordering Information
children.full_text:
Replacement units and accessories reference part numbers HX-7200-BASE (controller), PSU-2400 (power
supply), and CBL-ETC-3M (3-meter EtherCAT cable).

children.title: 8. Warranty
children.full_text:
The HX-7200 carries a 2-year limited warranty from date of installation, void if used with non-approved
power supplies (see Section 2.2) or if hard limit switches are bypassed (see Section 6).
